Compute observed-score ICCs for each rater pair

Source: R/api-pairwise-icc.R
pairwise_icc_table.Rd

Compare each pair on its common, complete units using a two-way ANOVA ICC. No MFRM fit, mixed-model estimation or extra package is required.

Usage

pairwise_icc_table(
  data,
  rater,
  unit,
  score,
  model = c("mixed", "random"),
  definition = c("agreement", "consistency"),
  type = c("single", "average")
)

Arguments

data

Long-format data with at most one row per rater and unit.

rater

Name of the rater identifier column.

unit

Names of columns jointly identifying a rated unit, for example c("Person", "Task", "Criterion"). These columns match observations; they are not separately estimated variance components.

score

Name of a numeric score column. Scores must share a meaningful interval scale. Numeric ordinal category codes do not establish that assumption. Factors/characters are not silently converted to scores.

model

"mixed" (default) describes the selected raters. "random" assumes raters were sampled from a population to which results may generalize. Two-way point formulas are identical; their interpretation differs. Choosing "random" does not establish random sampling.

definition

"agreement" (default) includes systematic rater offsets; "consistency" removes their contribution.

type

"single" (default) concerns one rating; "average" concerns the unweighted mean of the two ratings, not a mean over the full panel.

Value

A plain list containing table (one row per rater pair), anova (scaled ANOVA ingredients), cases (one row per pair and union of assigned units, with input-row references and inclusion flags), units (the unique input unit keys in input-column order), settings and notes. Unit in cases is a row index into units. Units assigned to neither member of a pair are outside that pair's audit. Missing1/Missing2 indicate explicit missing-score rows; Assigned1/Assigned2 also distinguish absent assignments. Save with base::saveRDS() and export data frames with utils::write.csv(). Reading saved output performs no calculation.

Details

All observed rater identifiers are paired. Each pair uses only units with two nonmissing scores. Other raters' missing scores do not exclude a unit for that pair. Missing-score rows and absent assignments are distinguished in cases. Duplicate rater-unit cells (including missing-score duplicates) are rejected rather than averaged. Identifiers must be nonmissing and nonblank. There is no imputation or observation weighting. Pairs with fewer than two complete units remain in table with an unavailable ICC.

Let R, C and E be the unit, rater and residual ANOVA mean squares on a complete n-by-2 matrix. Following Koo and Li (2016, Table 3), the numerator is R-E. The single-rating denominator is R+E for consistency, or R+E+2(C-E)/n for absolute agreement. The average-rating denominator is R for consistency, or R+(C-E)/n for agreement. Form records ICC(C,1), ICC(A,1), ICC(C,2) or ICC(A,2); interpret these together with Model. ICC(A,2) denotes an average of two ratings, not Shrout–Fleiss ICC(2,1). One-way ICCs are not computed.

Negative estimates are retained. A nonpositive denominator makes ICC unavailable and sets Status = "nonpositive_denominator"; RawICC retains the algebraic ratio when finite so it cannot masquerade as a valid reliability estimate. An entirely constant matrix is undefined, not 1. Internally scores are shifted and scaled to avoid overflow/underflow. anova records scaled mean squares, the offset/scale, numerator and denominator, so the calculation can be reconstructed. These scaled mean squares are not variances in the original score units.

Results describe each pair's retained unit mix. Different pairs can have different units and score ranges; their ICCs cannot automatically rank rater quality and should not be averaged into a panel ICC. Restricted unit variability can lower ICC without larger absolute disagreement. Inference requires a suitable sampling design and assumptions about errors and dependence. Treating several tasks from one person as separate units does not make them independent. No confidence intervals, hypothesis tests, quality bands or rater-training decisions are supplied. This is distinct from the component variance shares in compute_facet_icc(), MFRM separation reliability and the fitted expected agreement in interrater_agreement_table().

References

Koo, T. K., & Li, M. Y. (2016). A guideline of selecting and reporting intraclass correlation coefficients for reliability research. Journal of Chiropractic Medicine, 15(2), 155-163. doi:10.1016/j.jcm.2016.02.012 . Table 3; see also the 2017 erratum, doi:10.1016/j.jcm.2017.10.001 , correcting the one-way ICC(1,1) formula.

See also

interrater_agreement_table(), compute_facet_icc(), krippendorff_alpha_table(), score_comparison_table()

Examples

data("mfrmr_example_agreement", package = "mfrmr")
ratings <- mfrmr_example_agreement
absolute <- pairwise_icc_table(ratings, rater = "Rater",
  unit = c("Person", "Task"), score = "Score", definition = "agreement")
consistent <- pairwise_icc_table(ratings, rater = "Rater",
  unit = c("Person", "Task"), score = "Score", definition = "consistency")
absolute$table
#>   Pair Rater1 Rater2  N CandidateUnits ExcludedUnits       ICC    RawICC
#> 1    1     R1     R2 12             12             0 0.5925926 0.5925926
#> 2    2     R1     R3 10             12             2 0.8474576 0.8474576
#> 3    3     R2     R3 10             12             2 0.4807692 0.4807692
#>      Status         Model Definition   Type     Form
#> 1 available two_way_mixed  agreement single ICC(A,1)
#> 2 available two_way_mixed  agreement single ICC(A,1)
#> 3 available two_way_mixed  agreement single ICC(A,1)
consistent$table
#>   Pair Rater1 Rater2  N CandidateUnits ExcludedUnits       ICC    RawICC
#> 1    1     R1     R2 12             12             0 1.0000000 1.0000000
#> 2    2     R1     R3 10             12             2 0.8333333 0.8333333
#> 3    3     R2     R3 10             12             2 0.8333333 0.8333333
#>      Status         Model  Definition   Type     Form
#> 1 available two_way_mixed consistency single ICC(C,1)
#> 2 available two_way_mixed consistency single ICC(C,1)
#> 3 available two_way_mixed consistency single ICC(C,1)
# R1/R2 have perfect consistency, but R2's one-category offset reduces agreement.
# These ICCs treat 0--3 as numeric scores; justify equal score intervals.
